claimed_speedup: 52.93 GB/s on Intel vs xoshiro256+ 7.88 GB/s, RomuTrio 8.62 GB/s, wyrand 7.00 GB/s, ChaCha8 6.28 GB/s (xoshiro256+x8 40.18 GB/s)

tradeoffs: Requires AVX-512 (AVX512DQ, Skylake-X or newer); changes stream layout versus scalar PCG32.
caveats: README gives no CPU model, compiler or flags. Compared only against scalar PCG32, not std::mt19937.
name: simdpcg
workload: Filling an array of 50,000 32-bit random numbers (195 kB), cycles per element
claimed_speedup: scalar pcg32 4.25 cycles/op vs AVX-512 variants 2.37, 1.21 and 1.14 cycles/op
found_via: GitHub: lemire simdpcg (search 'lemire SIMD PCG vectorized random number generator')

tradeoffs: C++ port of lemire/simdpcg with SSE, AVX2 and AVX-512 paths and auto seeding.
caveats: Likely duplicate of simdpcg; README says 'see LICENCE file' and the license was not opened; no CPU or compiler stated.
name: SIMDpcg32_cpp
workload: Filling arrays with 32-bit random numbers, cycles per operation, SSE/AVX2/AVX-512 variants
claimed_speedup: scalar pcg32 3.1 cycles/op vs 1.6-1.3 (SSE), 2.1-1.6 (AVX256), 2.0-0.64 (AVX-512) cycles/op
found_via: GitHub: 'lemire SIMD PCG vectorized random number generator github simdpcg'

stars_or_usage: 125 stars; used by Yandex ClickHouse (per README)
tradeoffs: Needs Haswell+ AVX2 (AVX-512 for fastest path). xorshift128+ fails BigCrush per the README.
caveats: README gives no CPU model or compiler flags. Baseline is scalar xorshift128+, not xoshiro or mt19937; weak statistical quality.
name: SIMDxorshift
workload: Filling a 5000-element array of 32-bit random numbers (19 kB), cycles per element
claimed_speedup: scalar 3.63 cycles/op vs AVX 2.21, AVX variant two 1.88, AVX-512 variant two 1.47 cycles/op
found_via: GitHub: 'SIMD AVX2 AVX-512 vectorized xoshiro random number generator C++ library github'
WebSearch: arXiv new PRNG C++ faster than xoshiro256++ SIMD vectorized random number generator

hardware: x86-64, 16 CPUs (lscpu listing in README; model not captured here)
tradeoffs: 64-bit state, 64-bit output; period and jump/stream support are not those of xoshiro.
caveats: Very new, single-author design; self-reported quality (PractRand/BigCrush). lemire/testingRNG independently lists sirius64 at 4.29 GB/s vs pcg64 2.53 GB/s and mersennetwister 1.68 GB/s (GCC 14, Xeon Gold 6548N). Relative-speed table gives no absolute numbers.
name: Sirius64
baseline: xoshiro256++, xoshiro256**, PCG64 (RXS-M-XS and DXSM), xoroshiro128++, RomuTrio
workload: 64-bit PRNG throughput relative to splitmix64 (README comparison table), also corroborated in lemire/testingRNG
claimed_speedup: 99.6% of splitmix64 speed vs xoshiro256++ 78.7%, xoshiro256** 81.0%, pcg64 DXSM 57.8%, pcg64 RXS-M-XS 72.6%, RomuTrio 85.3%; ~5 cycles per 64-bit value
found_via: GitHub: 'github fast pseudo-random generator C passes BigCrush PractRand faster than xoshiro256++ new design'

hardware: Ryzen 7 1700 in a 2-core Ubuntu 20.04 VM
tradeoffs: Header-only; AVX2 gain only when four values are consumed together; four streams separated by 2^192 long jumps.
caveats: Rounded numbers, compiler/flags unstated. Compared only against its own serial version, not std::mt19937.
name: Xoshiro256PlusSIMD
workload: Generating 64-bit values four-wide with AVX2 vs serial
claimed_speedup: ~1 ns per value serial vs ~0.5 ns per value AVX2 four-wide (about 2x)
found_via: GitHub: 'SIMD AVX2 AVX-512 vectorized xoshiro random number generator C++ library github'

hardware: Intel Core i5-8250U
tradeoffs: Gist based on Vigna's xoshiro256++-vect-speed.c; eight interleaved streams; needs AVX2.
caveats: No license stated; compiler and flags unstated; single laptop CPU. Gist, not a repo.

name: Ginkgo
baseline: NVIDIA AmgX; MAGMA batched dense; MA57; LAPACK dgbsv
workload: GPU mixed-precision AMG, batched iterative solvers, sparse solves in AC-OPF

name: ISpMV
workload: GPU SpMV (fp64, alpha/beta variants, A and A^T) over 49 Mittelmann, 18 MIPLIB and 33 SuiteSparse large matrices on H100 PCIe.
claimed_speedup: 2.17x (Mittelmann), 1.64x (MIPLIB nnz>10M), 1.31x (SuiteSparse nnz>10M) geometric-mean speedup over cuSPARSE for alpha=1,beta=0
hardware: NVIDIA H100 PCIe 80GB, CUDA 13.4.2
license: MIT (interfaces, examples, benchmarks) plus proprietary ISpMV Binary License for compiled core
tradeoffs: Needs a one-time GPU preprocessing plan per matrix (37-110 ms geometric mean per direction); NVIDIA GPU only; core is a closed binary SDK.
caveats: Core is binary-licensed (not open source); compiler flags and CPU not stated; speedup values come from an LLM summary of the benchmark page, not verified row by row; baseline is cuSPARSE, not on the list. Mark low confidence.
found_via: GitHub: web search 'github sparse matrix-vector multiplication SpMV library faster than MKL Eigen SuiteSparse C++ benchmark'
